summary: The large-mimic recipe instead reaches a lichen touch. JS refuses AD_STCK before completing that turn. C enters mhitm_ad_stck and its magic-negation gate; port the whole sticking helper and wire its dispatch.

source.branch: A successful lichen AT_TUCH/AD_STCK hit reaches the monster-to-hero sticking branch; setting u.ustuck depends on magical cancellation, existing stuck state, and the defender sticks predicate.

evidence: nethack-c/upstream/src/uhitm.c:3306-3335 defines mhitm_ad_stck for all three actor combinations. It first computes mhitm_mgc_atk_negated. Hero-to-monster additionally requires a non-sticky adjacent defender; monster-to-hero emits hitmsg and requires no existing u.ustuck and a non-sticky defender. Barbed-devil messages are separate branches. Negation clears damage only for monster-to-monster.
js/uhitm.js:4967 leaves AD_STCK unported. The admitted baseline stops at zero-based segment 0 step 40 with simple monster action requires uhitm.c mhitm_ad_stck().

The frozen recording at segment 0 step 40 shows The lichen touches you!, a lichen F south of the hero, and the created large mimic still disguised as ] to the north. It records d(0,0)=0 at hitmu and rn2(10)=3 at mhitm_mgc_atk_negated(uhitm.c:87), establishing entry into the AD_STCK gate.

The recipe title does not identify the actual attacker. This prefix provides no large-mimic AD_STCK hit evidence. The absence of a helper-specific RNG label or stuck-state field does not establish that mhitm_ad_stck was skipped: the magic-negation draw comes from its first call. The screen alone does not serialize u.ustuck.

nethack-c/upstream/src/uhitm.c:80-99 compares rn2(10) with 3 * magic_negation(mdef), after attacker cancellation. mon.c:3421 owns set_ustuck. Port the complete helper and consume source-backed return values from its recursive dependencies; reuse the shared magic-negation helper only with direct completion evidence. Do not infer an allmain RNG defect from the truncated turn.
